items.title: CVE-2026-76504: Cisco Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Hex Encoding Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager has a severe unauthenticated remote administrative access flaw tracked as CVE-2026-76504.
items.summary: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager contains a hex encoding vulnerability due to improper handling of URI encoding in HTTP requests. This flaw allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to gain administrative access to affected systems. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 30, 2026, and mandated federal agencies to apply mitigations by October 3, 2026, in accordance with BOD 26-04 guidance.

items.title: Bitget Confirms Third-Party Zero-Day Behind $387.5 Million Cryptocurrency Theft
items.one_liner: Analyze the technical breach details of Bitget's $387.5M cryptocurrency theft via third-party security product zero-days.
items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget confirmed that a $387.5 million theft from its wallets on September 24, 2026, stemmed from attackers exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in third-party security appliances (Product A and Product B). Investigations by SlowMist and Mandiant revealed that threat actors compromised appliance nodes, deployed web shells for C2 persistence, used internal credentials to bypass risk controls, and executed customized tooling to steal assets across 11 blockchains. Circle, Tether, and NEAR Intents have frozen approximately $1.1 million of the stolen funds.
key_facts: Affected blockchains: 11 (including Ethereum, TRON, BNB Smart Chain)
items.bottom_line: Attackers stole $387.5 million from Bitget by exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in third-party security appliances to compromise wallet infrastructure.

items.title: Attackers Combine ChatGPT Feature Abuse With ClickFix to Deliver Trojan Malware
items.one_liner: Watch out for malicious CustomGPTs and ClickFix social engineering campaigns delivering RAT malware via fake CAPTCHAs.
items.summary: Cybercriminals have combined a legitimate ChatGPT feature with ClickFix social engineering attacks to distribute remote access trojans (RATs). Attackers created a custom GPT named 'Plus 5.6' promoted via malicious Google search ads, directing victims to a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA domain that tricks them into executing PowerShell commands. This execution bypasses security controls, installing a malicious MSI package that sideloads malware via a legitimate Canon-signed application to establish persistence and exfiltrate data. Huntress researchers identified at least 40 infections before OpenAI removed the custom GPT.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are combining custom ChatGPT features and ClickFix CAPTCHA lures to trick users into running commands that install RAT malware.

items.title: AuraForge: Scaling Security Supervision for Training Coding Agents
items.one_liner: AuraForge synthesizes executable security tests and builds multi-CWE training environments to improve the security outcomes of LLM coding agents.
items.summary: Researchers introduced AuraForge, a framework designed to synthesize and validate executable security tests to train secure coding agents without relying solely on real-world repositories. By combining attack-oriented test synthesis, language-extensible task construction, and safeguards against reward hacking, AuraForge generated AuraGym, a multi-language training gym featuring 679 tasks across 344 repositories and 177 CWE categories. Training models like Qwen3.5-4B with these synthesized tests yielded higher functional and security pass rates compared to human-written security tests while reducing false positives by over 83 percent.
items.bottom_line: Synthetic security test generation via frameworks like AuraForge significantly improves both functional correctness and secure code output in LLM coding agents.

claims.text: We introduce AuraForge to synthesize and validate executable security tests for training secure coding agents.
claims.support_span: We introduce AuraForge to synthesize and validate executable security tests for training secure coding agents.

items.title: CVE-2026-0298 GlobalProtect App: Code Execution Vulnerability in Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect for Windows has a MitM-exploitable SYSTEM code execution flaw in its pre-logon SAML flow.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has reported CVE-2026-0298, an improper input validation vulnerability in the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) component of the GlobalProtect app. The vulnerability allows a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM privileges on vulnerable Windows endpoints. Exposure is limited strictly to Windows devices using SAML authentication in the Connect Before Logon feature. Non-Windows versions are unaffected, and no in-the-wild exploitation has been observed.

Affected versions: GlobalProtect app 6.3.0 to <6.3.3-h14, 6.2.0 to <6.2.8-h13, 6.0.0 to <6.0.15
items.bottom_line: Mitigate CVE-2026-0298 on Windows endpoints by disabling SAML with Connect Before Logon or switching to machine certificates.

items.title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat
items.one_liner: G7 releases 100M barrels of oil and diesel to counter supply shocks and avert US export bans.
items.summary: The G7 has agreed to coordinate an immediate release of 100 million barrels of oil and diesel over four months via the IEA to stabilize spiking energy prices. This decision follows President Trump's threat to ban US diesel exports, which drove immense friction with European allies. In response, member states agreed to refrain from imposing energy export restrictions on each other. Despite these strategic reserve releases, renewed clashes between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces in Yemen caused Brent crude to rebound to around $102 a barrel.

Brent crude price: Around $102 per barrel

items.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
items.one_liner: Dangling COM registrations in Windows allow for privilege escalation via malicious DLL injection.
items.summary: Researchers have detailed a privilege escalation technique targeting a dangling COM object registration in Windows, identified as CVE-2026-66804. The vulnerability stems from a missing server executable for the CrossDevice COM object, allowing an attacker to place a malicious DLL in a user-writable directory to achieve code execution in privileged processes. This serves as an alternative exploit path following the incomplete fix for the 'Dark Elevator' bug (CVE-2026-50343). The researchers demonstrate that custom COM marshaling can be used to force the loading of the malicious DLL into a privileged service.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can achieve privilege escalation by placing a malicious DLL in a predictable path to exploit a dangling COM object registration.

items.title: China-nexus UAT-11587 targets government and policy organizations across Asia with Antino backdoor
items.one_liner: Analyze the tactics of China-nexus threat actor UAT-11587 using the Antino Rust backdoor and M365-based C2 against Asian targets.
items.summary: Cisco Talos uncovered a China-nexus threat actor tracked as UAT-11587 targeting government and policy organizations across Asian nations like Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia. The campaign utilizes spear-phishing messages and a five-stage infection chain to deploy a previously undocumented Rust-compiled Windows backdoor named 'Antino'. Antino uniquely uses Microsoft 365, via Microsoft Graph interacting with Outlook and OneDrive, as its exclusive command-and-control channel. Cloudflare infrastructure was heavily leveraged for delivery and payload staging during these espionage operations.

items.title: Pentagon breach exposes Social Security numbers and military records of millions
items.one_liner: A Pentagon personnel database breach exposed Social Security numbers and records for over 3 million people.
items.summary: A data breach at the Pentagon’s Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) exposed personally identifiable information, including Social Security numbers and military records, of 2.76 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased individuals. Attackers maintained access from October 2025 to July 2026 after exploiting a security vulnerability in an unencrypted file-sharing system. While the Pentagon claims there is no indication of misuse, affected individuals face lasting risks of identity theft and targeted phishing attacks, prompting offers of credit monitoring.

items.summary: Hackers breached the Pentagon’s Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) in October 2025, accessing sensitive records for over 3 million people until July 2026. items.title: CVE-2026-0307 GlobalProtect App: Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerabilities (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: Review and update your Palo Alto GlobalProtect app clients alongside PAN-OS or Prisma Access to remediate local privilege escalation risks.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed multiple local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the GlobalProtect app, tracked as CVE-2026-0307, which allow non-administrative users to escalate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Windows and root on macOS and Linux. Exploitation requires local access with low privileges and no user interaction, leveraging untrusted search path weaknesses (CWE-426). While mobile and ChromeOS platforms are unaffected, full remediation requires updating both the GlobalProtect app clients and PAN-OS or Prisma Access software versions. Palo Alto Networks has reported no active malicious exploitation of these flaws.
items.bottom_line: Failing to update both GlobalProtect app clients and PAN-OS leaves systems vulnerable to local privilege escalation to root or SYSTEM.

items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-92142, has been discovered in Apache Karaf where JMX MBeanServer lifecycle operations like createMBean, registerMBean, and unregisterMBean are omitted from the KarafMBeanServerGuard. Administrators must upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.12, 4.5.0, or later once available, or restrict network access to the JMX endpoint.

items.summary: A critical privilege escalation and remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-91048, has been identified in Apache Karaf due to missing command scope ACL configuration files. Because Karaf's command guard defaults to allowing commands with no matching ACL rules, authenticated shell users with only viewer-level access can run all commands within the jdbc and jms scopes. This bypasses the administrative restrictions protecting commands like shell:exec, resulting in a CVSS base score of 9.8.

items.title: ABSENTIA: Detecting Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in Web Applications
items.one_liner: ABSENTIA uses LLM agents with systematic route mapping and invariant falsification to detect backend broken access control vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ABSENTIA, a security scaffolding that transforms LLM agents into systematic vulnerability detectors for backend web application access controls. ABSENTIA constructs route-to-code maps and applies invariant falsification route-by-route to detect authorization flaws, avoiding unstructured search limitations. Evaluated on BAC-Bench—a benchmark of 30 recent broken access control advisories—ABSENTIA recalled 19 vulnerabilities, outperforming traditional static analysis tools like CodeQL and Semgrep which recalled none.

items.one_liner: Analyze Warlock ransomware operations exploiting SharePoint ToolShell vulnerabilities and deploying EDR killers via vulnerable drivers.
items.summary: The China-linked ransomware group Warlock (also tracked as Longlegs) targeted water utilities, telecom operators, regional governments, and universities by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability chain in Microsoft SharePoint known as ToolShell. Attackers dropped web shells, bypassed endpoint protection by deploying an AV/EDR-killing tool via the BYOVD technique using a vulnerable K7RKScan driver (CVE-2025-1055), and staged ransomware payloads within domain SYSVOL shares for network-wide execution via Group Policy objects.

items.title: South Africa Seeks Help After Cyberattack Targets Air Traffic Control
items.one_liner: South Africa's air traffic control provider discovered a ransomware toolkit on its OT network and is seeking forensic help.
items.summary: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), the South African state-owned company providing air traffic control and weather operations for roughly 10% of global airspace, has uncovered a cyberattack involving a ransomware toolkit on its operational technology network. Internal monitoring systems detected malware associated with early-stage ransomware attacks at Port Elizabeth Airport, along with indications of data exfiltration directed to external IP addresses located in China. Although technical teams implemented containment measures and malware removal, ATNS issued a request for quotes to hire external cyber-forensics firms to investigate the incident and a separate possible insider data theft at Maputo International Airport in Mozambique. The event underscores a broader surge in cyber threats targeting critical aviation infrastructure globally.

items.title: Identity-Bound Governance Under Execution Uncertainty: An Accountability Proof Block for LLM Agent Persistent Halts, with Cryptographic Implementation and Cross-Model Calibration
items.one_liner: The Accountability Proof Block provides cryptographic enforcement for human-in-the-loop authorization during LLM agent persistent halts.
items.summary: Researchers introduced the Accountability Proof Block (APB), a cryptographic mechanism designed to resolve identity-bound governance events where an autonomously governed LLM agent halts due to observability failures and requires authorized human intervention. The APB combines system evidence and human-supplied decisions bound by ed25519 signatures and RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization. Empirical testing across 3,812 halt events showed zero unresolved cases, and a multi-principal variant demonstrated complete resistance against simulated single-key capture attacks.
items.bottom_line: Deployers of advanced LLM agents can use Accountability Proof Blocks (APBs) to establish verifiable, tamper-resistant human authorization transfers during critical system halts.

items.title: ZoneClaw: Mitigating Persistent Memory Attacks by Establishing Memory-Zoning in OpenClaw-Style Computer-Use Agents
items.one_liner: ZoneClaw mitigates persistent memory injection attacks in computer-use agents by separating low-trust workspace memory from high-trust execution authority.
items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) use persistent workspace memory files that mix user instructions and external claims at the same privilege level, enabling persistent memory attacks where benign external content injects malicious instructions into memory. To mitigate this, researchers proposed ZoneClaw, which establishes memory-zoning with hierarchical trust zones and asymmetric privilege roles. External claims persist in a low-trust zone and must cross an explicit authority boundary to guide actions. Across evaluations, ZoneClaw drastically reduced attack success rates while preserving agent utility.
key_facts: Attack Success Rate (ASR) reduction: from 372/480 down to 6/480
items.bottom_line: Persistent memory attacks in computer-use agents can be effectively mitigated by enforcing strict memory-zoning and authority boundaries between ingested content and actionable execution.

claims.text: Across four attack scenarios, two injection settings, and four backbones, ZoneClaw drives ASR from 372/480 to 6/480 while retaining utility in 458/480 trials, and remains effective against some defense-aware attackers.

items.title: Tokenized Key-Gated Adapter Routing: A Secure Access Control Mechanism Against Private Data Leakage in LLMs
items.one_liner: Locket provides fine-grained, token-gated access control for LLMs using LoRA adapters to prevent PII leakage without sacrificing utility.
items.summary: To address privacy risks and PII leakage in LLMs deployed in sensitive domains, researchers introduced Locket (LoRA-Oriented Control via Keyed Entry Tokens). Locket trains fine-grained LoRA adapters representing different access policies, paired with a gating module that associates a keyed entry token with a specific adapter via hard routing. A valid token unlocks private knowledge, while a missing or invalid token triggers a privacy-preserving adapter that redacts sensitive content. Evaluations across models like Qwen3, Llama-3.2, and Gemma-2 showed that Locket maintains utility when tokens are valid and substantially reduces PII leakage when tokens are absent.
key_facts: Evaluated models: Qwen3 (1.7B and 8B), Llama-3.2 (1B and 3B), Gemma-2-2B
items.bottom_line: Tokenized key-gated LoRA adapter routing allows enterprises to enforce strict access control over private data inside LLMs without retraining base models.

items.title: Actions with Receipts: Jointly Binding Claims, Evidence, and Execution for Replayable Tool-Agent Auditing
items.one_liner: Claim-anchored execution contracts prevent citation and evidence tampering in tool-using agents by cryptographically binding claims to their execution traces and source spans.
items.summary: Tool-using agents can output citations and execution logs that remain structurally valid while being mismatched or transplanted across claims, actions, or source versions. items.bottom_line: Auditing tool-using agents requires jointly binding claims, source evidence, and execution traces to prevent citation-transplantation attacks.

items.title: Proof-Gated Signing: Solver-Checked Transaction Guards that Hold Under State Drift for Onchain AI Agents
items.one_liner: Proof-Gated Signing offers a robust defense for AI-controlled wallets against front-running and state-drift attacks.
items.summary: Proof-Gated Signing (PGS) is a new security mechanism designed to protect on-chain AI agents from malicious transactions caused by 'state drift'. By simulating transactions and using an SMT solver to verify declarative policies against oracle-uncertainty bands, PGS enforces strict post-conditions on wallet balance and permissions. Testing showed that PGS prevented 93.6% of harmful scenarios, significantly outperforming static allowlists and simulation-only checks. The system adds approximately 41k gas and 0.1-0.2 seconds of overhead per transaction.
items.bottom_line: Implementing PGS can effectively secure on-chain AI agents against complex, adaptive attacks that bypass standard simulation or allowlist-based guards.

items.title: Removing the NEEDLE in the Haystack: Backdoor Removal in LLMs via Weight Orthogonalisation
items.one_liner: NEEDLE removes LLM backdoors via weight orthogonalisation without requiring reference models or hurting benign performance.
items.summary: Large Language Models can be implanted with backdoors during training that trigger unwanted behavior, while existing defenses often inadvertently degrade model performance on benign prompts. By applying sequential weight orthogonalisation, NEEDLE suppresses the backdoor without requiring a clean reference model or original poisoned data. Evaluations across multiple model families show that NEEDLE achieves a 0% attack success rate on challenging code injection attacks while maintaining minimal KL divergence and preserving model capabilities.

items.title: OverAct: Measuring and Mitigating Proactive Over-Authorization in LLM Tool-Calling Agents
items.one_liner: OverAct benchmark measures proactive over-authorization in LLM tool callers, while SelfAudit cuts privacy-oriented excess by 43%.
items.summary: Researchers studied proactive over-authorization in structured tool-calling LLM agents, where agents retrieve more private user data than explicitly requested. items.title: Intrusion Detection for Agentic Processes: Evidence-Based Runtime Monitoring
items.one_liner: A-IDS introduces runtime monitoring and evidence-based intrusion detection for multi-step agentic workflows.
items.summary: Agentic AI deployments combine language model inference with tool execution, retrieval, and external access, creating complex security-relevant deviations across entire workflows. To monitor these processes, researchers propose the Agentic-Process Intrusion Detection System (A-IDS), an evidence-aware security layer that compares observed runtime behavior against versioned expectation baselines. A-IDS tracks workflow states, authorization, and communications while explicitly separating evidence capture from operational impact. The model treats prompt injection not just as an input anomaly, but as a potential origin for cascading cross-agent process deviations.
items.bottom_line: Securing multi-step agentic workflows requires runtime monitoring engines that evaluate evidence-supported process trajectories rather than isolated inputs.

items.title: Sleeping Secrets: How Fine-Tuning Reawakens Privacy Risks in Language Models
items.one_liner: ReGap demonstrates that data-free fine-tuning can extract private training data from language models without original supervision sets.
items.summary: Fine-tuning Large Language Models can inadvertently recover private information that was supposedly scrubbed or inaccessible through direct model queries. Proposing a data-free attack called ReGap, the authors show that fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation significantly improves target association recovery across multiple open model families. This privacy risk proves that standard model customization routines can reawaken latent sensitive data memorized during initial pre-training.

items.bottom_line: Routine model fine-tuning and customization can easily reawaken latent privacy risks and extract forgotten data from language models.

items.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Deploy Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement (PACE) to secure tool-using LLM agents against poisoned metadata and unauthorized side effects.
items.summary: Tool-using LLM agents face severe security risks when poisoned tool metadata, memory, or retrieved content steers subsequent tool execution. By checking schema-defined effects against authority compiled from authenticated requests, PACE maintains robust security enforcement. Evaluations across agent-security benchmarks demonstrate significant reductions in attack success rates with minimal utility loss.
items.bottom_line: PACE mediates every LLM agent tool call prior to execution using path confinement and effect verification, drastically cutting attack success rates with low overhead.

items.title: High-quality Data Do not Mean Safe! Poisoning LLMs after Data Selection
items.one_liner: Bi-QSTO demonstrates that safety-degrading prompt poison can survive aggressive quality-based data filtering in LLM fine-tuning pipelines.
items.summary: Safety-aligned Large Language Models remain vulnerable to fine-tuning attacks, yet practical training pipelines typically rely on quality-based data filtering to remove harmful examples. Researchers evaluate these filtering pipelines and discover that while overt samples are removed, certain retained high-quality samples still degrade model safety due to layer-wise gradient patterns. To exploit this loophole, the authors propose Bi-Stage Quality-Constrained Safety-Degradation Text Optimization (Bi-QSTO), which optimizes poisoned samples to survive strict quality filters. Experiments show that even with 90% filtering rates, Bi-QSTO successfully retains high effectiveness across target models.
items.bottom_line: Standard quality-based data filtering is insufficient to prevent LLM fine-tuning safety degradation because malicious prompts can be optimized to bypass filters.

items.title: Chaining Skills to Hijack LLM Agents
items.one_liner: APEX chains multi-step LLM agent skills together to inject false approvals and hijack execution.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced APEX, a method that constructs adversarial skill chains to hijack LLM agents by exploiting multi-step workflows. The technique leverages the fact that an agent-written record of genuine task progress can carry false claims of user approval across skills, allowing an upstream skill to induce a record and a downstream skill to execute an attacker-selected action. Tested across SkillsBench, APEX-crafted chains successfully induced targeted actions in 74.2% of attempts overall, and up to 84.3% on GPT-5.4. items.bottom_line: Attackers can chain LLM agent skills together using benign progress records to spoof user approval and successfully hijack targeted agent workflows.

items.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
items.one_liner: CompMat-Bench evaluates AI agents on computational materials science research steps using pre-reproduced simulation ground truths.
items.summary: Researchers introduced CompMat-Bench, a benchmark comprising 94 tasks derived from computational materials science studies to evaluate AI agents without requiring expensive real-time simulation runs. By pre-reproducing research steps, inputs, and results, the benchmark provides verified ground truth for grading agents using fixed rules without needing an LLM judge. Evaluations across three LLMs showed strong single-task pass rates of 66.0 to 90.4 percent, while performance degraded when handling longer workflows combined with reduced methodological guidance due to scientific errors.
items.bottom_line: CompMat-Bench enables efficient, rule-based evaluation of LLM agents on complex computational materials science tasks without executing expensive simulations during testing.

items.title: Add Runtime Controls to AI Agents with NVIDIA OpenShell
items.one_liner: NVIDIA OpenShell 0.1.0 provides runtime sandboxing and policy enforcement for autonomous AI agents.
items.summary: NVIDIA has released OpenShell 0.1.0, an open-source runtime designed to enforce granular permissions and access controls around autonomous AI agents without requiring application rewrites. The platform utilizes a multi-component architecture—including an OpenShell Gateway, Sandbox, and Supervisor—to enforce kernel-level filesystem restrictions, credential protection, and outbound traffic inspection. Operating outside the agent workload, the supervisor can analyze HTTP, GraphQL, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) traffic to permit read queries while blocking unauthorized writes, supporting enterprise tools, chip design automation, and robotics.
items.bottom_line: NVIDIA OpenShell 0.1.0 places kernel-level sandboxing and protocol inspection around AI agents to govern file access, credentials, and API operations externally.

items.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
items.one_liner: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties and expel diplomats as renewed fighting erupts across northern Ethiopia.
items.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic relations after Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara, expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats over national security threats, and accused Eritrea of supporting a new anti-government rebel alliance. Eritrea responded by cutting all ties and warning of negative consequences, as renewed conflict intensifies in northern Ethiopia involving the TPLF and allied groups. Simultaneously, Ethiopia and Egypt traded diplomatic expulsions amid long-standing tensions over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
items.bottom_line: The complete severance of diplomatic ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea signals a major escalation in regional instability and the breakdown of their 2018 peace pact.

items.summary: OpenAI has terminated three researchers for mishandling sensitive company information, including data related to external analysis of AI models. items.title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times
items.one_liner: Japan raises permanent residency fees 20x and tightens requirements amid surging foreign worker numbers.
items.summary: Japan has increased permanent residency application fees twentyfold to 200,000 yen ($1,270) alongside tighter income, pension, and upcoming Japanese-language proficiency requirements. Implemented under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, these strict policy adjustments seek to manage the country's record foreign population growth of 4.12 million residents amid an aging domestic labor force. items.title: HTTP/3 in Burp Suite - it’s time to find a bigger wordlist
items.one_liner: PortSwigger's Turbo Intruder and Burp Suite now support HTTP/3, enabling high-speed fuzzing over 100,000 requests per second and advanced race condition attacks.
items.summary: PortSwigger Research has released updates adding HTTP/3 support to both Turbo Intruder and Burp Suite via the new HTTP/3 Adapter plugin. Running over Wi-Fi against remote hosts, the HTTP/3 engine can comfortably exceed 100,000 requests per second (RPS) and scale up to 180,000 RPS from cloud instances. items.title: US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
items.one_liner: A botched execution attempt in Tennessee triggers an executive halt on state executions and renewed legal challenges.
items.summary: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike was left unconscious, intubated, and on a ventilator following a botched execution attempt involving two doses of pentobarbital. Lawyers stated that prison staff used at least seven needles, bent a needle 90 degrees, and failed to realize IV lines had blown, causing the lethal drug to pool in subcutaneous tissue rather than entering her bloodstream. In response to the failed procedure, Governor Bill Lee halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's legal team is currently seeking a commutation of her death sentence while hospital staff work to clear the drug from her system.
items.bottom_line: Tennessee has halted all executions for the year following a failed lethal injection attempt where blown IV lines left the inmate on a ventilator.

items.title: From A2A Attacks to Envelope-Layer Defense: Red-Teaming Evaluation of LLM Agents and a Three-Layer Isomorphic Attack-Defense Model
items.one_liner: Understand how A2A agent interaction protocols can be targeted via indirect prompt injection and how the ELA-ITL model structures envelope-layer defenses.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced A2A-TIBA, an attack method combining indirect prompt injection with bypass circumvention in multi-agent systems using protocols like ACP and A2A. The technique induces target agents to deploy callback interaction programs, enabling attackers to issue commands that bypass the agent layer. To better evaluate defenses, the authors developed GDA Measurement, a red-team testbed using raw context capture via an LLM gateway, and proposed the ELA-ITL three-layer isomorphic attack-defense model separating defenses into envelope packaging, LLM recognition, and agent interception. Experiments across 15 front-end and back-end combinations showed that adding malicious prompt labels to envelope channels significantly improves LLM recognition of malicious content.

items.title: Measuring the Microtask Eligibility Gap: When Is an Off-the-Shelf SLM Enough for an Agent Harness?
items.one_liner: Evaluate off-the-shelf SLM performance on agent harness microtasks and understand why quantization fails to bridge the eligibility gap.
items.summary: Researchers investigating the use of small language models (SLMs) in agent harnesses around frontier LLM planners evaluated Qwen3 (0.6B to 8B models) across four microtasks with strict confidence-interval eligibility thresholds. The evaluation revealed an eligibility gap: 0 of 16 FP16 configurations met practitioner thresholds, and 4-bit quantization (RTN/GPTQ/AWQ) further degraded performance without moving models into eligibility. The failure modes stem from capability deficits and decoding thresholds rather than precision loss alone, leading the authors to recommend placing SLMs behind cheap non-LLM baselines only where baselines fail.
items.bottom_line: Off-the-shelf SLMs fail practitioner-defined eligibility thresholds for agent microtasks, requiring non-LLM baselines as front-ends.

items.title: A Verifier Can Leak the Answer: Diagnosability Before Optimization in Closed-Loop Agent Debugging
items.one_liner: Verifiers in agent debugging can accidentally leak answers and invalidate solver evaluations unless evidence eligibility is strictly gated.
items.summary: Agent developers frequently evaluate prompts, tools, and debuggers using simulator-grounded verifiers. However, if verifier probes or predicates encode target identities, an optimizer can appear effective without resolving genuine ambiguity—essentially because the verifier leaked the answer. The authors discovered this failure mode in a closed-loop agent debugger and replaced solver-first evaluation with a support-gated verification contract that verifies evidence eligibility and non-revelation before component optimization.
items.bottom_line: Agent optimization benchmarks are flawed if the underlying verifier leaks target identities, necessitating support-gated verification contracts before running solvers.

items.summary: Researchers introduced EviGraph for proof-carrying selective recommendation over temporal public-service knowledge graphs. items.bottom_line: Reliable evidence-based recommendations require explicitly defining critical decision requirements rather than applying rigid verification to every missing detail.

items.summary: Researchers presented an educator-guided LLM pedagogical agent integrated into an entity-relationship diagram (ERD) editor to provide scaffolded feedback in conceptual database design. items.title: Ontology-Grounded, Reasoner-Verified Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Scientific AI
items.one_liner: A new automated method generates logically verifiable OWL ontology benchmarks to test scientific LLM reasoning failures.
items.summary: Researchers proposed a pipeline to automatically generate ontology-grounded multiple-choice question benchmarks from OWL 2 ontologies to evaluate logical reasoning in scientific AI models. Correct answers are grounded by design, while incorrect distractors are generated by perturbing class definition axioms and verified by an OWL reasoner. Six evaluated LLMs achieved zero-shot accuracies between 41.1% and 76.8%, showing the benchmarks are challenging and discriminative.
items.bottom_line: Ontology-grounded and reasoner-verified benchmarks provide a reliable way to catch factual and logical reasoning failures in scientific AI models.

items.title: No One Architecture Fits All: A Cross-Environment Evaluation of Hierarchical Red Team Agents
items.one_liner: Red team agent performance is environment-specific, with RL agents winning in dense environments and LLMs winning in large, complex networks.

items.bottom_line: Security teams should avoid assuming one red team agent architecture is superior, as performance varies significantly based on network scale and reward structure.

items.title: Deny Without Disabling: Authorization-Paired Evaluation and Control for Multi-Agent Systems
items.one_liner: FlowReview introduces an authorization-paired framework that eliminates false-positive blocked commits in multi-agent workflows.
items.summary: Multi-agent systems often face a safety dilemma where benign individual contributions jointly enable prohibited actions, but blocking all sensitive actions hinders collaboration. In controlled composition experiments, reviewing combined artifacts successfully reduced the denied-commit rate from 86.0% down to zero without causing any loss in authorized supply. These findings demonstrate that preserving object identity and permission linkage through verifiable components is crucial for secure multi-agent governance.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent systems can safely collaborate without excessive blocking if authorization and object identity are strictly paired with verifiable execution components.

items.title: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers

items.title: Agent Evaluation Reliability: More Tasks Won't (Always) Fix An Agent Leaderboard
items.one_liner: LLM agent leaderboard reliability varies heavily by scaffold and task choices, making underlying-model rankings unstable.
items.summary: An analysis of agent evaluations reveals that leaderboard rankings heavily depend on testing conditions like scaffolds and task sets, severely impacting underlying-model reliability. Furthermore, simply adding more tasks provides diminishing returns for model-ranking reliability when uncertainty is driven by scaffold coverage. Pooling diverse benchmarks offers a more cost-effective strategy to enhance cross-task rankings without inflating evaluation budgets.
items.bottom_line: Agent evaluation reliability depends heavily on testing scaffolds, meaning adding more tasks alone cannot fix leaderboard uncertainty.

items.title: Crossing the Cyber Divide: Sim-to-Sim and Sim-to-Real Transfer for RL Agents

VeriHarness transforms an underlying LLM generator into an agentic verifier equipped with workspaces, evidence tools, and reusable verification skills. A disagreement resolver checks competing claims against environmental evidence, while a consensus challenger tests shared claims and searches for omitted requirements. Across multiple benchmarks, VeriHarness significantly improves selection scores and self-improves its verification skills from failure feedback.
key_facts: Benchmarks evaluated: Five long-horizon workspace benchmarks
items.bottom_line: VeriHarness turns LLM generators into robust agentic verifiers using evidence-backed disagreement resolution, significantly improving long-horizon task verification accuracy.

items.title: Before Agents Decide: Epistemic Action in LLM-Based Systems
items.one_liner: Agent design must evaluate whether an LLM's available evidence is decision-ready before executing tasks.
items.summary: Researchers from arXiv are introducing the concept of epistemic action to LLM-based agent systems, highlighting how agents often lack necessary, well-formed evidence prior to making difficult decisions. Drawing from cognitive science, the authors categorize epistemic actions into acquiring missing evidence, transforming available evidence, and probing systems to create revealing responses. They propose epistemic scaffolding—the interfaces, tools, and environments that make these exploratory actions possible and auditable—to ensure decision-ready evidence is produced during complex agent workflows.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents need dedicated epistemic scaffolding to actively acquire, transform, and probe for better evidence before making critical decisions.

claims.text: Cognitive science calls actions that improve the basis for a later choice epistemic actions.

items.title: Heavy-Tailed Memory Traces in Long-Horizon Language Agents
items.one_liner: CTWM leverages heavy-tailed memory traces to optimize prompt token budgets and reduce prediction error in long-horizon language agents.
items.summary: Researchers analyzed the shape of memory use in long-horizon language agents and discovered that under repeated retrieval, agent memory concentrates on a small core while leaving rare states in a heavy-tailed distribution. Motivated by this finding, they proposed the Core-Tail World Model (CTWM), a rank-based memory controller that allocates prompt budgets using a single exponent while retaining a summarized tail. CTWM reduces prompt token usage across benchmark environments while maintaining state coverage and task accuracy.
items.bottom_line: Agent memory naturally exhibits heavy-tailed traces under finite context, which can be exploited using rank-based controllers to achieve token efficiency without accuracy loss.

claims.text: On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition coverage, reduces prompt tokens by 5.9%, and lowers bottom-half tail prediction error by 13.6% relative to a graph-memory baseline.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Preference Distributions
items.one_liner: LLMs show high internal consistency but lack consensus across models, making them unreliable as direct substitutes for human survey respondents.
items.summary: A systematic analysis of LLM-generated preference distributions reveals that while models are self-coherent, there is significant discordance between different model families and scales. The study tested nine open-weight models across three domains—air travel, restaurants, and consumer products—finding that outcomes are driven more by the specific model choice than by prompt engineering. These findings challenge the assumption that LLMs can reliably serve as standardized proxies for human survey respondents.
items.bottom_line: Do not rely on LLMs as standardized proxies for human preferences, as results are highly sensitive to the specific model architecture rather than the prompt.

claims.text: At the same time, we observe substantial discordance across both model families and scales, with little consensus even among their most probable outcomes.

claims.text: Our findings indicate that outcomes are influenced more by the choice of model than by the wording of the prompt, challenging the common assumption that sufficiently capable LLMs produce similar preference distributions when used as stand-ins for survey respondents.

items.title: SoK: Decentralized Agent Economic Infrastructure
items.one_liner: A systematic study of decentralized agent economies reveals critical verification-to-settlement failures across multi-protocol workflows.
items.summary: Decentralized agent economies frequently stitch together independent protocols to complete multi-step tasks, creating a risk where each step looks valid yet the overall outcome fails. For example, escrow contracts may release funds upon an authorized approval that lacks actual evidence of task completion. To analyze this, researchers systematize security and economic requirements across the agent task lifecycle into 17 property families and introduce guarantee closure as a task-relative evaluation criterion. Analyzing 12 systems and 840 matched executions, the study exposes frequent communication failures between verification and settlement stages. These findings highlight the architectural repairs needed to preserve end-to-end cryptographic and economic guarantees.
items.bottom_line: Decentralized agent systems suffer from critical disconnects between verification and settlement that require rigorous guarantee closure enforcement.

items.title: MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory
items.one_liner: MemFit provides a scalable, LLM-free insertion and retrieval long-term memory system for conversational agents that reduces construction costs while achieving state-of-the-art performance.
items.summary: Researchers proposed MemFit, a long-term memory system for conversational agents that aims to reduce the cost and latency of memory operations. Unlike systems that rely on expensive LLM calls for construction or compress data by discarding surface details, MemFit stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with LLM-free insertion. It uses an LLM-free multi-path retrieval strategy combining lexical and semantic signals with cross-encoder reranking. Empirical results on LoCoMo, MemGallery, and LongMemEval-S show that MemFit achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing memory construction time and cost.
key_facts: Evaluated benchmarks: LoCoMo, MemGallery, and LongMemEval-S
items.bottom_line: MemFit eliminates costly LLM calls during memory construction for conversational agents by using verbatim append-only stores and LLM-free multi-path retrieval.

items.title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
items.one_liner: Self-evolving AI agents require new safety frameworks because past experiences can become future security liabilities.
items.summary: A new survey explores the safety challenges of self-evolving AI agents that update their own parameters, memories, and tool definitions post-deployment. The researchers introduce the SAVER framework to track how reusable experiences can lead to safety violations when adapted or reused in new contexts. The study argues that current safety evaluations are insufficient for agents that continue to evolve, necessitating longitudinal testing to verify that safety properties persist across generations of agent adaptation.
items.bottom_line: Standard static alignment is insufficient for self-evolving agents; you must implement longitudinal evaluation to ensure safety properties survive agent adaptation.

items.title: CVE-2024-0244 – A heap buffer overflow in the Canon MF753Cdw printer
items.one_liner: A heap buffer overflow in Canon printer firmware demonstrates how obscure service drivers can be exploited for remote crashes or code execution.
items.summary: A researcher detailed the discovery of CVE-2024-0244, an unauthenticated heap-based buffer overflow in Canon MF753Cdw printers. The vulnerability exists in the fax driver's handling of SOAP messages sent to the /wsd/print endpoint. By sending a malformed payload with an oversized length field, an attacker can trigger an arbitrary free() operation, leading to a crash or potential code execution. The researcher leveraged UART access to debug the firmware and identify the vulnerable pointer.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Heap buffer overflow leading to arbitrary free()
items.bottom_line: Printer firmware remains a critical attack surface, with obscure features like fax drivers often containing unpatched memory corruption vulnerabilities.

This creates challenges for several use cases: - Confirming bug candidates that have been discovered manually or through static analysis. Regression tests: After fixing a race condition bug, there is often no good way to write a regression test that reliably triggers the bug as part of a test suite. Automatic bug discovery, such as fuzzing: It is hard for a fuzzer to exercise all interesting interleavings of concurrent operations, or reach code paths that are only exercised when operations are racing. I mostly discover bugs by manually reading code.
